hook: Ian Goodfellow studied computer science at Stanford University, earning undergraduate and masters degrees while working with Andrew Ng, before completing a PhD in machine learning at the Universite de Montreal in 2015 under Yoshua Bengio and Aaron Courville. While a graduate student he devised Generative Adversarial Networks, a framework in which two neural networks, a generator and a discriminator, are trained against each other so the generator learns to produce increasingly realistic data. He and his coauthors described the idea in a 2014 paper that became one of the most influential works in deep learning and gave rise to a large body of research on image synthesis and generative modeling. After completing his PhD he continued this line of research at OpenAI, contributing to work on improving the stability of GAN training. He also co-authored the widely used textbook Deep Learning with Bengio and Courville, published by MIT Press in 2016.
